title: The Ĝ Infrared Search for Extraterrestrial Civilizations with Large Energy Supplies. V. When Galaxies Glow with Industry
comment: 34 pages, 16 figures, 4 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the most robust stellar population synthesis (SPS)-based search for galaxy-spanning technological waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies spanning a wide range of spectral energy distribution (SED) types, including ultraluminous IR galaxies and MIR-luminous active galactic nuclei (AGN). We incorporate the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis code at the stellar population level, so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently to Dyson sphere reprocessing. With \texttt{Prospector}, we perform a suite of 1,419 injection recovery tests across a range of covering fractions, $α$, where we successfully recover the injected covering fractions (best-fit slope $m = 0.92$) and detect them through Bayesian model selection down to $α\sim 4$--$5\%$ in quiescent galaxies. None of our 129 galaxies prefer a Dyson sphere component, and we place the first per-galaxy 95\% upper limits on warm ($T_{\rm BB} \gtrsim 100$K) swarms, reaching a median $α< 0.3\%$ across quiescent hosts without a dominant AGN. Our injection-calibrated detection rates convert these zero detections into a population bound of $<2.6\%$ of galaxies hosting $α= 25\%$ swarms ($95\%$ confidence). Because survey colors cannot separate waste heat from starbursts and AGN, we develop a scaffold for future searches, running from inexpensive archival screens such as the Balmer decrement and the stellar-to-dynamical-mass offset a swarm leaves behind, through resolved fitting with nuclear excision, to PRIMA FIR photometry that makes targeted JWST imaging decisive. We find that the outskirts of quiescent galaxies are the best hunting grounds for future technosignature searches.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the most robust stellar population synthesis (SPS)-based search for galaxy-spanning Dyson sphere waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies. Using injection recovery tests, they detect Dyson sphere components down to covering fractions of 4-5% but find zero detections, yielding population upper limits of <2.6% of galaxies hosting 25% coverage swarms, and propose a multi-tier search scaffold targeting quiescent galaxy outskirts.
AI.motivation: To search for extraterrestrial technosignatures by identifying galaxy-spanning Dyson sphere waste heat, using more robust SPS-based methods than previous surveys that could not cleanly separate waste heat from natural astrophysical processes like starbursts and AGN.
AI.method: Incorporates the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis code at the stellar population level so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently. Uses Prospector to perform 1,419 injection recovery tests across covering fractions, applies Bayesian model selection to 129 nearby galaxies, and develops a scaffold for future searches using archival screens, resolved fitting with nuclear excision, and PRIMA FIR photometry.
AI.result: Successfully recovers injected covering fractions (slope m=0.92) and detects them down to alpha~4-5% in quiescent galaxies. No galaxies prefer a Dyson sphere component. Places first per-galaxy 95% upper limits on warm swarms with median alpha<0.3% for quiescent hosts. Converts zero detections into population bound of <2.6% of galaxies hosting 25% coverage swarms at 95% confidence.
AI.conclusion: The outskirts of quiescent galaxies are the best hunting grounds for future technosignature searches. Survey colors alone cannot separate waste heat from natural sources, so a multi-tier observational scaffold is needed—from inexpensive archival screens through resolved fitting to JWST imaging guided by PRIMA FIR photometry.

title: Recycled Gas Dominates the Metal-rich Fuel of Supermassive Black Holes
comment: 14 pages, 1 table, 4 figures
summary: Understanding the origin and chemical properties of gas accreted by supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is essential for linking black hole growth to galaxy evolution. Using a suite of 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations, we investigate the chemical properties of gas accreted onto SMBHs in massive galaxies with stellar masses of $10^{10.9-11.9}\,\rm M_\odot$ and black hole masses of $10^{8.5-9.7}\,\rm M_\odot$ at $z=0$. By tracing the full cosmological histories of individual gas particles, we identify their origins and enrichment pathways. The accreted gas is classified into four categories: ``early'' gas accreted during the early assembly phase of the main halo, ``external'' gas originating from other galaxies or subhalos, ``recycled'' gas enriched through stellar evolution processes within the primary galaxy, including asymptotic giant branch (AGB) winds and supernova ejecta, and ``smooth'' gas accreted from the intergalactic medium. We find that recycled gas dominates the accretion budget and is already metal rich at early epochs. Gas from other origins typically undergoes gradual chemical enrichment within the galactic environment prior to black hole accretion. The mean abundance ratios show only weak redshift evolution and are broadly compatible with the high metallicities inferred for quasar broad-line regions. Our results suggest that metal-rich gas supply to SMBHs arises naturally from cosmological galaxy evolution and stellar recycling.

AI.tldr: Using 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations, this study traces the chemical origins of gas accreted by supermassive black holes in massive galaxies, finding that recycled gas from stellar evolution dominates the accretion budget and naturally supplies metal-rich material compatible with quasar broad-line region metallicities.
AI.motivation: Understanding the origin and chemical properties of gas accreted by supermassive black holes is essential for linking black hole growth to galaxy evolution.
AI.method: The study uses a suite of 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations targeting massive galaxies with stellar masses of 10^10.9-11.9 Msun and black hole masses of 10^8.5-9.7 Msun at z=0. Individual gas particles are traced through their full cosmological histories to identify origins and enrichment pathways. Accreted gas is classified into four categories: early, external, recycled (from AGB winds and supernova ejecta), and smooth (from the intergalactic medium).
AI.result: Recycled gas dominates the accretion budget and is already metal-rich at early epochs. Gas from other origins typically undergoes gradual chemical enrichment within the galactic environment before black hole accretion. Mean abundance ratios show only weak redshift evolution and are broadly compatible with the high metallicities inferred for quasar broad-line regions.
AI.conclusion: Metal-rich gas supply to supermassive black holes arises naturally from cosmological galaxy evolution and stellar recycling processes.

title: Why is GN-z11 Bright, Compact, and Nitrogen Enhanced? Insights from UV Absorption and Emission Diagnostics
comment: 22 pages, 11 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: We investigate the UV spectrum of GN-z11, a luminous, compact galaxy with strong nitrogen lines, at $z=10.60$, using deep JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra assembled from the JADES, SPURS, and GO programs. After optimized reduction and extraction of the IFU data including an evaluation of statistical and systematic uncertainties, we obtain mutually consistent spectra from the high- and medium-resolution observations. After carefully accounting for the data quality limitations, we identify prominent P-Cygni profiles in NV$λ\lambda1238,1243$, SiIV$λ\lambda1394,1403$, and CIV$λ\lambda1548,1550$, together with broad NIV]$λ\lambda1483,1486$ emission (FWHM $\sim1600$ km s$^{-1}$). The P-Cygni profiles resemble those of massive stars such as O-type stars and luminous blue variables (LBVs), while the broad NIV] emission resembles that of nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) stars. We fit stellar and active galactic nuclei (AGN) UV spectral models and find that the stellar models are strongly preferred over the AGN models ($Δ$WAIC $=-25$), with the preference driven primarily by the NV P-Cygni profile. These results indicate that the luminous, compact UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars. We derive electron densities from CIII]$λ\lambda1907,1909$, NIII]$λ\lambda1747-1754$, and NIV], with the nitrogen diagnostics extending well beyond the CIII]-based limit and reaching densities of $\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ for NIV], indicating physically distinct carbon- and nitrogen-emitting nebular components. These findings suggest that the apparent nitrogen enhancement inferred for GN-z11 as a whole may arise when strong narrow nitrogen emission originates from dense gas locally enriched in nitrogen by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec observations of GN-z11 at z=10.60 reveal P-Cygni profiles in NV, SiIV, and CIV with broad NIV] emission, consistent with massive stars (O-type, LBV, WN) rather than AGN. Stellar models are strongly preferred over AGN models, and high electron densities from nitrogen diagnostics indicate locally nitrogen-enriched dense gas around WN stars, explaining the apparent nitrogen enhancement without requiring an AGN.
AI.motivation: GN-z11 is a luminous, compact galaxy at z=10.60 with strong nitrogen lines, and the origin of its UV continuum (massive stars vs. AGN) is debated. Understanding whether its spectral features come from stars or an AGN is crucial for interpreting early galaxy properties and its apparent nitrogen enhancement.
AI.method: The authors used deep JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra from JADES, SPURS, and GO programs, with optimized reduction and extraction. They identified P-Cygni profiles (NV, SiIV, CIV) and broad NIV] emission, fit stellar and AGN UV spectral models using WAIC comparison, and derived electron densities from CIII], NIII], and NIV] diagnostics.
AI.result: Stellar models are strongly preferred over AGN models (ΔWAIC = -25), driven primarily by the NV P-Cygni profile. Electron densities from nitrogen diagnostics reach ≳10^6.5 cm^-3 for NIV], much higher than the CIII]-based limit, indicating separate carbon- and nitrogen-emitting nebular components.
AI.conclusion: The UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars, not an AGN. The apparently enhanced nitrogen may arise from dense gas locally enriched by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region, rather than requiring an AGN contribution.

title: FLAGS II: Constraining Galaxy Formation Models with Dimensionality Reduction of Direct Observables
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Comparisons between observations of galaxies and theoretical predictions are regularly performed using physical properties, which are inferred by the often slow and biased process of SED fitting. Forward modelling facilitates a reliable alternative, whereby models are evaluated using direct observables alone. However, these datasets become high-dimensional when collating observations from multiple telescopes, leading to sparse sampling, memory intensity and visualisation difficulties. We show that 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes, constructed using the non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm UMAP, preserve sufficient information to differentiate between five models. Using a simple $χ^{2}$-like metric, we show that JAGUAR reproduces the population of bright galaxies $(m_{\mathrm{AB}}<26)$ in GOODS-S six times as well as SC-SAM and twelve times as well as SAGE. By adjusting the hyperparameters, we quantify how well each model replicates the distribution of SED shapes. The template SED approach of SPRITZ and the lack of photoionisation in SAGE cause significant discrepancies, highlighting the importance of comprehensive forward modelling. The embedded position of each galaxy can be identified $>100$ times faster than inferring its properties with Bayesian SED fitting, making this approach an ideal alternative for deriving statistical model constraints from large surveys such as LSST and Euclid, and performing simulation-based inference with CAMELS.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a forward-modelling approach using UMAP-based 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes to compare galaxy formation models with observations, avoiding slow SED fitting. This method differentiates between five models, shows JAGUAR best reproduces bright galaxies in GOODS-S, and is over 100 times faster than Bayesian SED fitting.
AI.motivation: Traditional SED fitting used to compare galaxy observations with theoretical models is slow, biased, and suffers from high-dimensionality issues when combining multi-telescope data. The authors aim to provide a fast, reliable alternative using forward modelling with direct observables.
AI.method: The authors use UMAP, a non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm, to construct 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes. They compare five galaxy formation models using a chi-squared-like metric and tune hyperparameters to assess how well each model replicates the distribution of SED shapes.
AI.result: UMAP embeddings preserve enough information to distinguish between five models. JAGUAR reproduces bright galaxies (m_AB<26) in GOODS-S six times better than SC-SAM and twelve times better than SAGE. The embedded position of a galaxy can be identified over 100 times faster than Bayesian SED fitting.
AI.conclusion: The UMAP-based forward-modelling approach is an efficient alternative to SED fitting for deriving statistical model constraints, particularly suitable for large upcoming surveys like LSST and Euclid, and for simulation-based inference with CAMELS.

title: Magnus mountains on spinning neutron stars
comment: 19 pages, 12 Figures. Comments welcome
summary: We investigate the formation of a "Magnus mountain'' on a neutron star, arising from the non-axisymmetric Magnus force acting on the elastic crust by pinned superfluid vortices. Such a deformed star would act as a source of continuous gravitational waves. We consider a compressible two-component stellar model and solve the coupled equations of motion for the fluid and elastic components self-consistently, allowing the stellar deformation and the resulting mass quadrupole to be determined. For simplicity, we model the star as an infinitely long cylinder, consisting of a fluid region with a thin ocean and crust. We find that the current quadrupole is zero, while the Magnus forces are strong enough to produce (dimensionless) mass quadrupoles as large as $\sim 10^{-5}$, and so would be limited only by the finite strength of the vortex pinning and the breaking strain of the star's elastic crust. Such large deformations are promising from the point of view of the detection of continuous gravitational waves by current and future detectors, and motivate further work on more realistic stellar models.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the "Magnus mountain" formation on a neutron star due to non-axisymmetric Magnus forces from pinned superfluid vortices acting on the elastic crust. Using a compressible two-component stellar model (infinitely long cylinder with fluid interior, thin ocean, and crust), the authors find the current quadrupole vanishes while dimensionless mass quadrupoles can reach ~1e-5, limited only by vortex pinning strength and crust breaking strain. Such deformations are promising for continuous gravitational wave detection.
AI.motivation: Neutron stars are promising sources of continuous gravitational waves, and understanding the mechanisms that deform them—such as the Magnus force from pinned superfluid vortices—is crucial for predicting detectable gravitational wave emission.
AI.method: The authors construct a compressible two-component stellar model, treating the star as an infinitely long cylinder consisting of a fluid region with a thin ocean and elastic crust. They solve the coupled equations of motion for the fluid and elastic components self-consistently to determine the stellar deformation and resulting mass quadrupole.
AI.result: The current quadrupole is found to be zero, while the Magnus forces can produce dimensionless mass quadrupoles as large as ~1e-5, limited solely by vortex pinning strength and the crust's breaking strain.
AI.conclusion: The large deformations predicted are promising for detecting continuous gravitational waves with current and future detectors, motivating further investigation using more realistic stellar models.

title: Trace the Self-Gravitating Gas Using CO Isotopologues
comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, accepted by ApJ
summary: Recent studies have shown that the star formation rate (SFR) correlates tightly and linearly with the mass of gravitationally bound gas, which can be delineated from the power-law tail of the column-density probability distribution function ($N$-PDF) derived from dust emission observations. This relationship holds across four orders of magnitude within the Milky Way--spanning low-mass to high-mass star-forming regions and encompassing the extreme environment of the Central Molecular Zone. Building on this framework, we present a new approach for estimating the mass of gravitationally bound gas in molecular clouds using multi-line CO isotopologue observations. Our sample includes 16 molecular clouds with robust detections in $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O $J$ = 1-0, spanning both massive inner Galaxy clouds and nearby star-forming regions. We find that the $N$-PDFs derived from combined CO isotopologue data recover the characteristic log-normal plus power-law profiles seen in dust-based studies. The mass and spatial distribution of the self-gravitating structures estimated from both dust-based and CO-based methods agree well throughout the sample. This indicates that the CO isotopologue combination can robustly trace the self-gravitating component via the $N$-PDF method and provides a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for identifying the star-forming gas in molecular clouds.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a novel method to estimate the mass of gravitationally bound gas in molecular clouds using multi-line CO isotopologue observations (12CO, 13CO, C18O J=1-0), validated against dust-based N-PDF methods across 16 molecular clouds. The CO-based approach recovers the characteristic log-normal plus power-law N-PDF profiles and agrees well with dust-based estimates of self-gravitating mass and spatial distribution, offering a scalable, velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission.
AI.motivation: The SFR correlates tightly with the mass of gravitationally bound gas, which can be traced via the power-law tail of the column-density PDF derived from dust emission. However, dust-based methods lack velocity information and may have resolution limitations, motivating the need for a complementary tracer that can identify self-gravitating gas while providing kinematic information.
AI.method: The authors construct N-PDFs from combined CO isotopologue observations (12CO, 13CO, and C18O J=1-0) for 16 molecular clouds, spanning massive inner Galaxy clouds and nearby star-forming regions. They compare the resulting column-density PDFs and the mass/spatial distributions of self-gravitating structures against those derived from dust emission-based methods.
AI.result: The N-PDFs from CO isotopologue combinations reproduce the characteristic log-normal plus power-law profile seen in dust-based studies. The mass and spatial distribution of self-gravitating structures derived from CO-based and dust-based methods agree well across the entire sample, demonstrating that CO isotopologues can robustly trace the self-gravitating component.
AI.conclusion: The CO isotopologue combination provides a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for identifying and quantifying star-forming (self-gravitating) gas in molecular clouds via the N-PDF method, extending the framework of SFR-bounded gas correlation to kinematic-based tracers.

title: Synchrotron and Inverse-Compton Signatures of Black to White Hole Explosions: Weibel-Mediated External Shocks in the Interstellar Medium
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures,2 tables
summary: We study the non-thermal electromagnetic counterpart expected when the relativistic, near-isotropic ejecta of a black-to-white hole transition sweep up the interstellar medium (ISM). Building on a photospheric model for the prompt $γ$-ray emission~\cite{Villani2026}, we parametrize the kinetic energy available for an external shock, $\eiso=R_k\egprompt$, and model the resulting collisionless forward shock with a Weibel-mediated field~\cite{Weibel1959,MedvedevLoeb1999,SironiSpitkovsky2011}. We estimate the synchrotron and synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission from shock-accelerated electrons in a one-zone, Thomson-regime approximation, including inverse-Compton cooling, Klein-Nishina suppression, self-absorption, and $γ$-$γ$ opacity, all at order-of-magnitude or first-order accuracy. For illustrative parameters ($\egprompt\sim10^{44}$ erg, $R_k=0.1$, $Γ_0=100$), the electrons are slow-cooling, so for $p=2.5<3$ the synchrotron spectrum peaks at the cooling frequency $ν_c$, in the MeV-to-GeV range and softening with time; the afterglow evolves in a fraction of a second to tens of seconds -- orders of magnitude faster than a classical long-duration GRB afterglow at comparable energy, density, and Lorentz factor -- with duration, peak energy, and flux depending sensitively on $R_k$, $\nism$, and $\epse,\epsB,\xie$. We identify parameter regions where a 1 keV photon-count estimate, below the intrinsic peak, exceeds a nominal detection threshold, and discuss features -- a fast, faint, roughly isotropic transient after a hard-spectrum prompt flash, without an achromatic jet break -- that may distinguish this scenario from short GRBs, magnetar giant flares, and other fast transients, while flagging the assumptions (forward-shock-only dynamics, one-zone Thomson-regime radiation, an illustrative detectability criterion) limiting its quantitative reach.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the non-thermal electromagnetic afterglow expected from the relativistic, near-isotropic ejecta of a black-to-white hole transition sweeping up the ISM. Building on a photospheric prompt γ-ray model, the authors model the collisionless forward shock with Weibel-mediated magnetic fields and estimate synchrotron and SSC emission including cooling, Klein-Nishina suppression, self-absorption, and γ-γ opacity at order-of-magnitude accuracy. For illustrative parameters, the afterglow peaks in the MeV-GeV range, evolves over fractions of a second to tens of seconds (far faster than classical GRB afterglows), and may be distinguishable from short GRBs and other fast transients by its fast, faint, roughly isotropic nature without an achromatic jet break.
AI.motivation: The aim is to characterize the external-shock afterglow counterpart of a black-to-white hole (BH-to-WH) transition, a speculative scenario in quantum-gravity alternatives to classical black holes. Since such transitions may produce relativistic near-isotropic ejecta, predicting their electromagnetic signature is crucial for identifying and distinguishing these events in transient surveys against known classes like short GRBs and magnetar giant flares.
AI.method: The authors parametrize the kinetic energy of the external shock as E_iso = R_k E_γ,prompt, building on a photospheric model for prompt γ-ray emission. They model the collisionless forward shock with a Weibel-mediated magnetic field and compute synchrotron and synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission in a one-zone, Thomson-regime approximation. They include inverse-Compton cooling, Klein-Nishina suppression, synchrotron self-absorption, and γ-γ opacity, all at order-of-magnitude or first-order accuracy. Parameter studies explore R_k, n_ISM, ε_e, ε_B, and ξ_e to map detection-relevant regions.
AI.result: For illustrative parameters (E_γ,prompt ~ 10^44 erg, R_k = 0.1, Γ_0 = 100), electrons are slow-cooling; for p = 2.5 < 3 the synchrotron spectrum peaks at the cooling frequency ν_c in the MeV-to-GeV range, softening with time. The afterglow evolves over fractions of a second to tens of seconds — orders of magnitude faster than classical long GRB afterglows — with duration, peak energy, and flux sensitive to model parameters. Parameter regions exist where a 1 keV photon-count estimate exceeds a nominal detection threshold.
AI.conclusion: The BH-to-WH afterglow would appear as a fast, faint, roughly isotropic transient following a hard-spectrum prompt flash, lacking an achromatic jet break. This combination of features may distinguish it from short GRBs, magnetar giant flares, and other fast transients. The quantitative reach is limited by assumptions including forward-shock-only dynamics, one-zone Thomson-regime radiation modeling, and an illustrative detectability criterion.

title: CLASSY. XV. Kinematics and Spatial Distributions of Outflows in Local Highly Star-Forming Galaxies
comment: Accepted to ApJ, 15 pages, 5 figures
summary: Star-forming galaxies drive massive outflows that play an important role in galaxy evolution by regulating feedback and influencing the dynamics of surrounding media. Measuring galactic outflow rates is essential for quantifying feedback efficiency and the amount of mass, momentum, and energy deposited into the circumgalactic medium. In this paper, we examine 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey with radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines presented in M. Huberty et al. (2024), to study their spatial distributions and kinematic properties. We study the SiII, SiIII, and SiIV ionization states that trace the cool and warm phases of the outflows and find that SiII traced winds generally behave differently than the warmer SiIII and SiIV traced winds. We derive the mass, momentum, and energy loading factors, which we find scale inversely proportional to stellar mass. We find that our measurements of the mass and momentum loading factors are in agreement with the hydrodynamic FIRE-2 simulations. We model the velocity profiles of the winds, with profiles reaching a maximum velocity of 620 km/s on average, in agreement with hydrodynamic simulations from CGOLS. We also investigate the relationship between outflow properties and the age of the stellar population from SED fitting. We find that outflows associated with young star forming regions are more likely to have a column density dominated by cooler gas and have mass outflow rates which decrease with radius.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey using radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines to study spatial distributions, kinematic properties, and loading factors across different stellar masses and stellar population ages.
AI.motivation: Quantifying galactic outflow rates is essential for understanding feedback efficiency and the mass, momentum, and energy deposited into the circumgalactic medium, which plays a critical role in galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines (SiII, SiIII, SiIV) tracing cool and warm outflow phases, applied to 17 outflows from the CLASSY survey, combined with SED fitting for stellar age determination and comparison with FIRE-2 and CGOLS hydrodynamic simulations.
AI.result: SiII-traced winds behave differently from warmer SiIII/SiIV-traced winds; mass, momentum, and energy loading factors scale inversely with stellar mass and agree with FIRE-2 simulations; wind velocity profiles reach a maximum of ~620 km/s on average, consistent with CGOLS; outflows from young star-forming regions are cooler gas-dominated with mass outflow rates decreasing with radius.
AI.conclusion: Galactic outflow properties vary with ionization state and stellar population age, with loading factors inversely scaling with stellar mass and showing consistency with state-of-the-art hydrodynamic simulations.

title: Microscopic Interaction versus Purely Gravitational Coupling in Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Dark Matter: A One-Fluid and Two-Fluid Comparison
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables
summary: In this study, we investigate strange quark stars (SQSs) admixed with scalar dark matter (DM), focusing on the role of microscopic interactions versus purely gravitational coupling. Our results demonstrate that while the interacting one-fluid model yields viable configurations with M_TOV > 2M_sun that satisfy current pulsar M-R measurements alongside the tidal deformability (Lambda) constraints from GW170817, the noninteracting two-fluid model more robustly meets both existing GW170817 limits and the tighter Lambda bounds anticipated from next-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates strange quark stars admixed with scalar dark matter, comparing interacting one-fluid and noninteracting two-fluid models against pulsar and gravitational-wave constraints.
AI.motivation: To understand how microscopic interactions versus purely gravitational coupling between strange quark matter and scalar dark matter affect the viability and observable predictions of strange quark star configurations.
AI.method: The authors model strange quark stars admixed with scalar dark matter using two approaches: an interacting one-fluid model (with microscopic interactions between components) and a noninteracting two-fluid model (purely gravitational coupling). They then compare predicted masses, radii, and tidal deformabilities against observational constraints.
AI.result: The interacting one-fluid model produces viable configurations with maximum TOV masses exceeding 2 solar masses and satisfies current pulsar mass-radius measurements and GW170817 tidal deformability constraints. However, the noninteracting two-fluid model more robustly satisfies both existing GW170817 limits and the tighter Lambda bounds expected from next-generation gravitational-wave detectors.
AI.conclusion: The noninteracting two-fluid treatment of dark matter-admixed strange quark stars is more robust against both current and anticipated future gravitational-wave constraints, suggesting that purely gravitational coupling between strange quark matter and scalar dark matter may be the more observationally favored scenario.

title: Ripples in the OCEANS: Broad Line Variability of Little Red Dots
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a unique class of compact, red sources discovered in the JWST extragalactic deep fields. Determining if they are indeed powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is one of the main drivers of the intense study of these objects. Evidence for variability in these objects provides a direct test for the active galactic nucleus (AGN) nature of their central engine. In this study, we present a variability analysis of 6 LRDs observed by the $R \sim 2700$ OCEANS survey and leverage archival $R \sim 1000$ spectroscopic data from the CEERS and RUBIES surveys. We report marginal detections of $\rm Hα$ broad-line (BL) variability in the LRDs OCEANS-100424/RUBIES-42232 (27\% variability at 2.1$σ$ significance) and OCEANS-35829/RUBIES-49140 (GlimmIr/Irony; 50\% variability at 1.5$σ$ significance). The other 4 LRDs in our sample do not show evidence for BL variability, with a 1$σ$ upper limit of $4.8 \% - 30\%$ variability between their epochs of observations. We also find no evidence ($<1σ$) for continuum variability in our LRD sample. We compare our results to a sample of SDSS-RM quasars to determine the probability of our broad $\rm Hα$ variability detections. We find that the probability of reproducing 2 variable and 4 nonvariable quasars is $4.71\%$, corresponding to $\sim 2 σ$ departure from typical quasar variability. The detection of BL $\rm Hα$ variability in 2 LRDs provides some evidence for the AGN nature of these objects as opposed to pure scattering models.

AI.tldr: A variability analysis of 6 Little Red Dots (LRDs) using OCEANS and archival CEERS/RUBIES spectroscopy finds marginal broad Hα variability in 2 LRDs (27% at 2.1σ and 50% at 1.5σ), no continuum variability, and a ~2σ departure from typical quasar variability expectations, providing some evidence for the AGN nature of these objects.
AI.motivation: Little Red Dots are a newly discovered class of compact red sources in JWST deep fields. Determining whether they are powered by accreting supermassive black holes is a major open question. Variability provides a direct, time-domain test of the AGN nature of their central engines, as opposed to alternative explanations like scattering models.
AI.method: The authors analyze 6 LRDs from the OCEANS survey (R~2700) combined with archival R~1000 spectroscopic data from CEERS and RUBIES. They measure broad-line Hα variability between epochs and continuum variability, comparing the observed variability detections to a control sample of SDSS-RM quasars.
AI.result: Marginal broad Hα variability is detected in 2/6 LRDs: OCEANS-100424 (27% variability at 2.1σ) and OCEANS-35829 (50% variability at 1.5σ). The other 4 LRDs show no BL variability (1σ upper limits of 4.8%-30%). No continuum variability is found (<1σ). Comparison with SDSS-RM quasars gives a 4.71% probability of reproducing 2 variable and 4 nonvariable sources, a ~2σ departure from typical quasar variability.
AI.conclusion: The detection of broad Hα variability in 2 LRDs provides partial evidence supporting the AGN interpretation for these objects, favoring accretion-powered central engines over pure scattering models, though the significance is modest.

title: Interacting Supernovae: a Radio and X-ray Strategy to Constrain the Structure of the Circumstellar Medium
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures, comments welcome
summary: The interaction of supernova (SN) ejecta with the dense circumstellar medium (CSM) converts shock kinetic energy into radiation across multiple wavebands. We investigate the dependence of the X-ray and radio emission on the CSM geometry, considering spherical, hourglass, and disk shapes for the CSM. We find that the spectral and light-curve properties, both in X-ray and radio, significantly differ for spherical and non-spherical CSM structures. For a non-spherical CSM, the radio light curve flattens out near the peak frequency, due to efficient free-free absorption by the unshocked CSM. Moreover, the early rise of the radio light curve is shallower when the CSM density along the observer line of sight is larger than that in other directions. If the CSM density is lower along the observer line of sight, the radio light curve flattens near its peak, and the reverse-shock component is negligible in X-rays. Building on these features, we provide a method to constrain the CSM structure based on the rising part the radio light curve in the proximity of its peak; we show that the decay part of the radio light curve, after its peak, carries insight on whether the CSM density profile is wind-like or not. We further adopt the X-ray signal to corroborate the information extracted from radio. We test our strategy on SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf. For both SNe, we find that an asymmetric CSM is in excellent agreement with radio and X-ray observations and provides a viable alternative to non-wind scenarios suggested in the literature. Our findings highlight the crucial insight provided by radio and X-ray signals into the mass-loss history of the SN progenitor.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how the geometry of the circumstellar medium (CSM) surrounding supernovae affects X-ray and radio emission. Comparing spherical, hourglass, and disk CSM shapes, the authors find that non-spherical CSM produces distinct observable signatures in radio and X-ray light curves (e.g., flattening near the radio peak due to free-free absorption, a shallower rise when CSM density is higher along the line of sight). They develop a method to constrain CSM structure from the radio light curve's rise and decay, corroborated by X-ray data, and validate it on SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf, finding that asymmetric CSM best explains the observations.
AI.motivation: To understand how the geometry of the CSM surrounding supernovae affects multi-waveband (X-ray and radio) radiation, since non-spherical CSM structures—which reflect realistic progenitor mass-loss histories—may be misinterpreted as spherically symmetric in existing models, leading to incorrect inferences about the progenitor's mass loss.
AI.method: The authors model SN ejecta interacting with CSM of three geometries (spherical, hourglass, disk) and compute the resulting X-ray and radio emission. They analyze how light-curve and spectral properties depend on CSM geometry and observer orientation, then devise a diagnostic method based on the shape of the rising and decaying portions of the radio light curve near its peak. X-ray emission is used as corroborating evidence. The strategy is tested against observational data from SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf.
AI.result: Non-spherical CSM yields radio light curves that flatten near the peak frequency due to efficient free-free absorption by the unshocked CSM. The early radio rise is shallower when CSM density along the line of sight is higher than elsewhere; if lower along the line of sight, the radio light curve flattens near its peak and the reverse-shock X-ray component is negligible. For SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf, asymmetric CSM matches both radio and X-ray observations well, offering a viable alternative to the non-wind scenarios previously suggested in the literature.
AI.conclusion: The rising and decaying parts of the radio light curve around its peak encode crucial information about CSM geometry and density profile (wind-like vs. non-wind-like), with X-ray emission providing corroboration. The results emphasize that radio and X-ray observations offer a powerful probe of the SN progenitor's mass-loss history, and that assuming spherical CSM symmetry can lead to incorrect physical interpretations.

title: Observing Co-Located Neutral and Ionized Gas-Phase Iron Depletion in the Magellanic Clouds
summary: Depletion is the observed phenomenon where gas-phase elemental abundances are reduced through accretion onto dust grains. We measure neutral gas-phase elemental abundances (S, Fe) in the Magellanic Clouds along 33 sightlines using high-resolution UV spectroscopy (HST/COS and HST/STIS), and compare them to ionized gas-phase abundances (S, Fe) adopted from the literature for six co-located H\,\textsc{ii} regions (with the furthest separation of $\lesssim3'$, 50 pc). Comparing S abundances show that S is minimally depleted in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions and surrounding diffuse ISM. However, we find that the gas-phase Fe abundances in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be lower than those of the neighboring neutral ISM by 0.3 to 2 dex. This difference is likely an offset in the amount of Fe depleted into dust grains. As accretion of gas-phase Fe is likely not effective at the temperatures of the H\,\textsc{ii} regions, Fe depletion into solid form would have occurred in the dense atomic or molecular clouds prior to star formation. Stronger depletion in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions shows that Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in the first few million years following ionization. Our observations highlight that Fe depletion in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be a useful tracer of Fe depletion in dense molecular clouds, which are challenging to observe directly via UV absorption.

AI.tldr: The paper measures gas-phase S and Fe abundances in the Magellanic Clouds along 33 sightlines using UV spectroscopy, comparing neutral ISM abundances to those in co-located H II regions. While S shows minimal depletion in both environments, Fe abundances in H II regions are 0.3–2 dex lower than in the neighboring neutral ISM, indicating that Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in young H II regions and that H II region Fe depletion can serve as a proxy for dense molecular cloud depletion.
AI.motivation: To understand dust depletion processes in different ISM phases and to use H II region Fe depletion as a tracer for depletion in dense molecular clouds, which are difficult to observe directly via UV absorption.
AI.method: High-resolution UV spectroscopy (HST/COS and HST/STIS) of 33 sightlines to measure neutral gas-phase S and Fe abundances in the Magellanic Clouds, compared with literature ionized gas-phase abundances from six co-located H II regions (separation ≤ 3 arcmin, ~50 pc).
AI.result: S is minimally depleted in both H II regions and the diffuse ISM. Fe abundances in H II regions are found to be 0.3 to 2 dex lower than in the adjacent neutral ISM, suggesting stronger Fe depletion into dust in H II regions.
AI.conclusion: Fe depletion into dust must have occurred in dense atomic/molecular clouds prior to star formation (since accretion is ineffective at H II region temperatures), and Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in the first few million years after ionization. H II region Fe depletion can serve as a useful tracer of Fe depletion in dense molecular clouds.

title: 3D Radiative Transfer of Lyman-series Lines with SKIRT
comment: 12 pages, 13 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary:
Context. High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy and polarimetry provided by XRISM and IXPE offer new diagnostics of the geometry and kinematics of photo-ionised plasmas around compact objects. Interpreting reprocessed X-ray emission in such systems requires full three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) including photon-ion interactions.
  Aims. We extend the Monte Carlo (MC) RT code SKIRT by implementing the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, enabling self-consistent modelling of resonance scattering, radiative recombination, and polarisation of these lines in X-ray photo-ionised plasmas.
  Methods. We implemented Lyman-series transitions (up to $n=10$) for ions with $Z=$1--30, including fine-structure splitting and linear polarisation in resonance scattering. Two channels for the production of the Lyman-series lines (resonance scattering and radiative recombination) are considered.
  Results. The implementation reproduces analytical expectations and shows good agreement with Cloudy. The SKIRT simulations naturally capture RT effects such as P Cygni profiles and line-profile distortion in optically thick media, which are inaccessible to the conventional 1D RT codes commonly used in X-rays. In 3D geometries, we find that anisotropic illumination and velocity fields significantly modify the Lyman series line ratios and profiles, all of which are observable with XRISM.
  Conclusions. The extended version of SKIRT provides a powerful framework for interpreting X-ray line spectra and polarisation from photo-ionised plasmas. It is particularly suited for constraining the geometry and velocity structure in the vicinity of compact objects in the XRISM and IXPE era.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT by implementing Lyman-series lines of H-like ions (Z=1-30, up to n=10), including fine-structure splitting and polarisation, for self-consistent 3D modelling of resonance scattering and radiative recombination in X-ray photo-ionised plasmas around compact objects. The implementation is validated against Cloudy and analytical expectations, and captures 3D RT effects such as P Cygni profiles and line-profile distortion in optically thick media that are inaccessible to 1D codes, providing a powerful framework for interpreting XRISM and IXPE observations.
AI.motivation: High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy and polarimetry from XRISM and IXPE provide new diagnostics of geometry and kinematics of photo-ionised plasmas around compact objects, but interpreting reprocessed X-ray emission requires full 3D radiative transfer including photon-ion interactions, which existing codes cannot handle.
AI.method: The authors extend the Monte Carlo RT code SKIRT by implementing Lyman-series transitions (up to n=10) for H-like ions with Z=1-30, including fine-structure splitting and linear polarisation in resonance scattering. Two production channels are modelled: resonance scattering and radiative recombination.
AI.result: The implementation reproduces analytical expectations and agrees well with Cloudy. SKIRT captures 3D RT effects such as P Cygni profiles and line-profile distortion in optically thick media. In 3D geometries, anisotropic illumination and velocity fields significantly modify Lyman series line ratios and profiles, all observable with XRISM.
AI.conclusion: The extended SKIRT provides a powerful framework for interpreting X-ray line spectra and polarisation from photo-ionised plasmas, particularly suited for constraining geometry and velocity structure near compact objects in the XRISM and IXPE era.

title: Gaia parallax bias via spherical harmonics: A Python tool and discussion of possible causes
comment: Submitted. The parallax-correcting code in Python and graphical presentation is available at https://zenodo.org/records/21708614
summary: Parallaxes in Gaia DR3 are known to suffer from a complex set of sky-correlated and magnitude-dependent offsets or biases at the level of a few tens of $μ$as. Estimated from a sample of one million distant quasars and AGNs from the CRF catalog, the average offset is negative, but the actual distribution of this important parameter shows significant variations on the sky. We propose a practical method to evaluate the parallax correction as a function of sky position and, optionally, of $G$ magnitude using a spherical harmonic series, and supply a tested Python tool {\tt varpi3.py} available on Zenodo\footnote{ https://zenodo.org/records/21708614}. We find that only the constant $Y_{00}$ term is significantly dependent on magnitude, while the other 80 harmonic terms are either close to zero or flat with magnitude. The directions of the smallest and largest parallax offsets are $(l,b)\simeq(220\degr,+43\degr)$ and $(l,b)\simeq(45\degr,-45\degr)$, which are close to the orientation of the quasar density dipole reported in recent publications. Motivated by this curious coincidence, we review possible physical effects resulting in a negative bias of measured parallaxes, including an anisotropic universe with a positive curvature and an orbital aberration component. The proposed method of parallax correction is tested using independent asteroseismology data for four different areas on the sphere. Finally, we show that the parallax zero-point propagates into the CRF proper-motion field through the parallax--proper-motion covariance, biasing the vector spherical harmonic determination of the secular-aberration glide, and hence the Galactocentric acceleration, at the microarcsecond-per-year level.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces varpi3.py, a Python tool using spherical harmonics to correct Gaia DR3 parallax zero-point offsets that vary across the sky and with G magnitude, based on a sample of one million quasars from the CRF catalog. The tool reveals that only the constant term varies with magnitude, identifies polar directions of smallest/largest offsets correlated with the quasar density dipole, and demonstrates that uncorrected parallax biases propagate into CRF proper-motion fields via parallax-proper-motion covariance, affecting secular aberration measurements.
AI.motivation: Gaia DR3 parallaxes suffer from systematic, sky-correlated, and magnitude-dependent biases at the tens of microarcsecond level. A robust, practical correction method as a function of position (and optionally magnitude) is needed to enable precise astrometric science.
AI.method: The authors model the parallax zero-point offset using a spherical harmonic series (81 terms) fitted to one million distant quasars/AGNs from the CRF catalog, and package the method as varpi3.py. They analyze magnitude dependence of harmonic coefficients, correlate directions of extreme offsets with known quasar density dipoles, and test the correction using independent asteroseismology data. They also derive the propagation of parallax bias into proper-motion fields via parallax-proper-motion covariance.
AI.result: Only the Y00 (constant) term depends strongly on magnitude; other harmonic terms are near zero or flat in magnitude. The smallest and largest parallax offsets occur near (l,b) ≈ (220°, +43°) and (45°, −45°) respectively, aligned with the quasar density dipole. The correction is validated with asteroseismology data across four sky regions, and parallax zero-point bias is shown to affect secular-aberration glide and Galactocentric acceleration at the μas/yr level.
AI.conclusion: The proposed spherical-harmonic-based parallax correction, delivered as varpi3.py, provides an accurate, practical way to remove sky- and magnitude-dependent Gaia DR3 parallax biases. The results also highlight a potential physical connection between parallax zero-point structure and an anisotropic universe with positive curvature or orbital aberration, and underscore the importance of parallax correction for proper-motion-based cosmology and Galactic dynamics measurements.

title: How Neutron Star Radii Encode the Dense-Matter Equation of State and Hadron-Quark Transition
comment: 15 pages including 7 figures
summary: We investigate how future high-precision neutron star (NS) radius measurements encode microscopic information about the dense-matter equation of state (EOS), focusing on a possible first-order hadron--quark phase transition and the resulting mass--radius topology. Within a Bayesian framework using meta-model EOSs with nine microscopic parameters, we analyze mock radius measurements $R_{1.4}=11.9\pmσ_R$ km with $σ_R=0.9$ and $0.1$ km for canonical NSs. We introduce inverse EOS--radius mappings that give the posterior mean of each EOS parameter as a function of $R_{1.4}$. Their slope measures radius sensitivity, while their curvature determines the leading precision dependence of the posterior mean through the Jensen expansion. Resolving the mappings into four mass--radius topologies, Connected, Disconnected, Both, and No-Quark-Matter, reveals a clear hierarchy of information. The symmetry-energy parameters $L$ (slope) and $K_{\rm sym}$ (curvature) are strongly encoded in $R_{1.4}$ and their posterior means shift appreciably with improved radius precision, whereas the higher-order hadronic parameters show stronger topology dependence. Among the transition parameters, the transition density $ρ_t$ is the most strongly encoded in $R_{1.4}$, while the energy-density jump and quark-matter sound speed are more strongly associated with the topology of the full mass--radius sequence. Since the different topologies have strongly overlapping $R_{1.4}$ distributions, even precise radius measurements cannot by themselves identify the topology or uniquely determine the high-density transition properties. These results provide a parameter-dependent hierarchy for assessing the scientific return of future high-precision radius measurements and complementary probes of high-density

AI.motivation: To understand what microscopic information about the dense-matter equation of state can be extracted from future high-precision neutron star radius measurements, and to establish a parameter-dependent hierarchy for assessing the scientific return of such measurements, especially regarding the possibility of a hadron-quark phase transition.
AI.method: Uses a Bayesian framework with meta-model EOSs parameterized by nine microscopic parameters. Analyzes mock radius measurements R_1.4=11.9±σ_R km with σ_R=0.9 and 0.1 km. Introduces inverse EOS-radius mappings giving posterior means of each EOS parameter as a function of R_1.4, using slope for radius sensitivity and curvature for precision dependence via the Jensen expansion. Resolves mappings into four mass-radius topologies (Connected, Disconnected, Both, No-Quark-Matter).

Higher-order hadronic parameters show stronger topology dependence. Transition density ρ_t is most strongly encoded in R_1.4, while energy-density jump and quark-matter sound speed are more associated with the full mass-radius topology. AI.conclusion: Future high-precision radius measurements provide strong constraints on symmetry-energy parameters (L, K_sym) and transition density, but cannot uniquely identify the mass-radius topology or determine all high-density transition properties. title: SPURS: Massive Stars, Dense Gas, and Ly$α$ Escape in GN-z11 at $z = 10.6$
comment: Main text 35 pages, 20 figures
summary: We present ultra-deep {\it JWST} spectroscopy of GN-z11 ($z=10.6$) obtained through the SPURS Cycle 4 Large Program, providing the deepest rest-UV view yet obtained of a galaxy at $z>10$. GN-z11 was previously found to be nitrogen-enhanced with detectable Ly$α$. The SPURS spectrum reveals P-Cygni stellar wind features and broad He II emission that are jointly reproduced by stellar population models incorporating very massive stars (VMS; $>100\,M_\odot$) at low metallicity and young ages ($\lesssim3$ Myr). We also detect a broad ($\rm FWHM=1670$ km s$^{-1}$) component to N IV] $\lambda1486$, now seen in several nitrogen emitters, potentially arising from dense WN winds or LBV-like outbursts associated with a population of VMS in a dense environment, though an AGN-driven wind cannot be excluded. In either scenario, this broad component may trace the gas producing GN-z11's nitrogen enhancement. Rest-UV absorption lines reveal a fast ($\sim500$~km~s$^{-1}$), highly ionized outflow and a negligible neutral gas covering fraction. We resolve the weak Ly$α$ emission (EW=5.6 Å, $f_{\rm esc,Lyα}=2.7$\%), finding a broad red wing (44\% of flux at $>500$ km s$^{-1}$) that should experience reduced IGM damping wing suppression and help explain Ly$α$ visibility at $z>10$. Fine-structure O I* $\lambda1304$ emission indicates dense neutral gas near a subset of the ionizing sources, which may also scatter Ly$α$ to the large observed velocities. The weak low-ionization absorption favors a picture in which this dense neutral gas is confined to a compact nuclear region. Together, these results are consistent with a rapid burst of star formation building up the dense nuclear regions and surrounding clusters in GN-z11.

AI.tldr: Ultra-deep JWST spectroscopy of GN-z11 (z=10.6) reveals P-Cygni features and broad He II emission consistent with very massive stars (>100 M☉), a broad N IV] component, a fast highly ionized outflow with negligible neutral gas covering fraction, and resolved weak Lyα emission with a broad red wing, pointing to a rapid star formation burst building dense nuclear regions.
AI.motivation: To obtain the deepest rest-UV view yet of a galaxy at z>10, GN-z11, to investigate its nitrogen enhancement, Lyα visibility, and the physical processes (e.g., very massive stars, outflows, AGN) driving its unusual properties.
AI.method: Ultra-deep JWST spectroscopy via the SPURS Cycle 4 Large Program, analyzed using stellar population models incorporating very massive stars at low metallicity, along with measurements of emission/absorption line profiles, widths, equivalent widths, escape fractions, and outflow kinematics.
AI.result: P-Cygni features and broad He II require VMS at young ages (<3 Myr); a broad N IV] component (FWHM=1670 km/s) may arise from WN winds/LBV outbursts or AGN; a fast (~500 km/s) highly ionized outflow with negligible neutral gas covering; Lyα has EW=5.6 Å, f_esc=2.7%, with 44% of flux in a broad red wing reducing IGM damping; O I* emission indicates dense neutral gas confined to a compact nuclear region.
AI.conclusion: GN-z11's properties are consistent with a rapid burst of star formation building up dense nuclear regions and surrounding clusters, with very massive stars playing a key role in producing the observed nitrogen enhancement, outflows, and Lyα visibility at z>10.

title: An Evolving Leptonic Jet Model for Delayed Radio Flares in Neutrino Blazars
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, submitted to PRD
summary: The jets of blazar active galactic nuclei (AGN) are promising sites of hadron acceleration and subsequent neutrino production, owing to their extreme intrinsic power and high radiation density. Potential associations of IceCube neutrinos with blazars displaying delayed radio flares, such as TXS~0506+056 and PKS~1424+240, may support this scenario. However, the mechanisms and location of particle acceleration in the jet remain unclear. The 2017 IceCube event associated with TXS 0506+056 was concurrent with the initial peak of a flare in gamma rays, followed by a longer flare at radio frequencies peaking three years later. State-of-the-art single-zone radiative source models focus on the compact high-energy-emitting region, and thus fail to describe this subsequent radio enhancement. In this work, we model the time-domain multi-frequency evolution of TXS 0506+056 by considering electron emission along the physically extended jet. We couple a numerical particle interaction framework with a dynamic description of the temporal and spatial jet evolution down to the parsec scale. We fit the model to multi-wavelength data, including multi-frequency radio light curves. The results suggest that the parsec-scale jet meets a population of older, cooled electrons near the edge of the observable radio core, establishing a causal relation between the initial high-energy emission and trailing radio activity. This spatially and temporally resolved modeling approach can offer new insights into the physical conditions along the jet of flaring neutrino candidate blazars.

AI.tldr: The paper models the time-domain multi-frequency evolution of the blazar TXS 0506+056 by simulating electron emission along the physically extended jet, coupling particle interaction with spatial and temporal jet dynamics down to parsec scales. Fitting to multi-wavelength data reveals that the parsec-scale jet encounters a population of older, cooled electrons near the edge of the observable radio core, establishing a causal link between initial high-energy emission and delayed radio flares.
AI.motivation: The 2017 IceCube neutrino event associated with TXS 0506+056 was concurrent with a gamma-ray flare followed by a delayed radio flare peaking three years later. Existing single-zone radiative models focus on the compact high-energy-emitting region and fail to explain this subsequent radio enhancement, motivating a spatially resolved modeling approach.
AI.method: The authors couple a numerical particle interaction framework with a dynamic description of temporal and spatial jet evolution down to the parsec scale, modeling electron emission along the physically extended jet. The model is fit to multi-wavelength data, including multi-frequency radio light curves.
AI.result: The fits suggest that the parsec-scale jet encounters a population of older, cooled electrons near the edge of the observable radio core, establishing a causal relation between the initial high-energy emission and trailing radio activity.
AI.conclusion: This spatially and temporally resolved modeling approach can provide new insights into the physical conditions along the jet of flaring neutrino candidate blazars, addressing limitations of single-zone models.

title: ALMA observations of pre-JWST z ~ 10 galaxy candidates: A CO(J = 9-8) line from a ULIRG at z = 2.54 and revisit of the photometric redshifts with JWST photometry
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures (7 in Appendices), MNRAS in press
summary: We present Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) observations targeting the [OIII]$88\,μ$m line for six $z\sim10$ galaxy candidates selected with the Hubble Space Telescope and the Spitzer Space Telescope. We detect a line ($4.5σ$) and dust continuum emission ($30σ$) in UDS_18697, while detecting neither robust line nor continuum emission in the remaining five objects. The detected line in UDS_18697 is identified as CO($J=9-8$), because follow-up James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRSpec observations have confirmed the redshift as $z=2.54$. UDS_18697 is classified as an ultra luminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG) with far-infrared (FIR) luminosity of $L_\mathrm{FIR}\approx1.1\times10^{12}\,L_\odot$, assuming a dust temperature of $T_\mathrm{d}\approx42\,$K, estimated using a physically-motivated method. We find that UDS_18697 follows the $L_\mathrm{FIR}-L'_\mathrm{CO}$ relation for local and $z>2$ galaxies, albeit being slightly brighter in CO($J=9-8$). Also, based on the follow-up NIRSpec observations and spectral energy distribution fitting using JWST/NIRCam photometry, we found that most of our targets are suggested to be low-$z$ interlopers. Motivated by these redshift misclassifications, we investigate colour--colour selection criteria for high-$z$ galaxies using JWST spectroscopic survey catalogues. We find that elevating a colour threshold tracing the Lyman break is crucial for constructing a robust high-$z$ sample, particularly for wide field surveys such as Euclid Deep Fields and Roman High-Latitude Wide-Area Survey.

AI.tldr: ALMA observations targeting [OIII] 88 μm lines in six z~10 galaxy candidates reveal that only one (UDS_18697) shows a 4.5σ line and 30σ dust continuum, which follow-up JWST/NIRSpec data identify as a z=2.54 ULIRG rather than a z~10 object. The remaining candidates are mostly low-redshift interlopers according to JWST data. The paper then investigates color-color selection criteria to improve high-z galaxy selection for future wide-field surveys.
AI.motivation: To verify the nature of z~10 galaxy candidates selected via HST/Spitzer photometry using ALMA observations, given that such high-redshift samples are prone to contamination by low-redshift interlopers.
AI.method: ALMA observations targeting the [OIII] 88 μm line and dust continuum in six z~10 candidates; follow-up JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy and NIRCam photometry for redshift confirmation; spectral energy distribution fitting; and color-color selection criteria analysis using JWST spectroscopic survey catalogs.
AI.result: Only UDS_18697 shows robust detections (line at 4.5σ, continuum at 30σ), identified as CO(9-8) at z=2.54 via JWST NIRSpec—a ULIRG with L_FIR≈1.1×10^12 L_sun at T_d≈42 K. Most other targets are low-z interlopers. Raising the Lyman-break color threshold is critical for constructing robust high-z samples for surveys like Euclid Deep Fields and Roman.
AI.conclusion: Photometrically selected z~10 candidates are highly susceptible to low-z contamination; ALMA+JWST follow-up is essential for verification, and refined color-color selection criteria (particularly Lyman-break thresholds) are needed for future wide-field high-z surveys.

title: Cross-spectral Analysis of the Type-C Quasi-periodic Oscillation Shoulder Component in GX 339-4
comment: 17 pages, 19 figures (including appendices). Accepted for A\&A
summary: We revisit Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) observations of GX~339$-$4 during the rising phase of its 2006/2007 outburst and apply a joint power-density-spectrum (PDS)--cross-spectrum (CS) decomposition to the type-C quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) region. Within this framework, the QPO region is described by a narrow QPO fundamental and a neighboring high-frequency shoulder, whose amplitudes and phase lags can be measured separately. The shoulder is first detected at MJD~54142.04, mainly through the imaginary part of the CS and a narrow local structure in the phase-lag spectrum, before becoming a resolved high-frequency shoulder in the PDS. It follows the QPO frequency evolution on the high-frequency side, with $R_ν=ν_{\rm sh}/ν_{\rm QPO}\simeq1.04$--$1.18$. The QPO lag remains small, typically below $\sim0.17$~rad, whereas the shoulder carries a larger hard lag of $\sim0.5$--$0.8$~rad. Energy-resolved fits show the same separation: the QPO lag is close to zero or only weakly positive across most of the energy band, while the shoulder lag is systematically larger and generally increases with photon energy. The two components have broadly similar rms--energy shapes, although their relative strengths evolve during the observed sequence. Although the shoulder remains broad, with $Q\sim2$--$4$, its lag and rms--energy behavior resemble those of the type-B QPO detected shortly after our observations. This similarity raises the interesting possibility that the shoulder is related to an earlier, broader stage of the variability later seen as the type-B QPO.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits RXTE observations of GX 339−4 during the 2006/2007 outburst rise, applying a joint PDS–CS decomposition to the type-C QPO region. It identifies a narrow QPO fundamental and a distinct high-frequency shoulder with separate amplitudes and phase lags. The shoulder first appears at MJD 54142.04, tracks the QPO frequency (R_ν ≈ 1.04–1.18), carries a larger hard lag (~0.5–0.8 rad) than the QPO (<0.17 rad), and its energy-dependent behavior resembles that of the type-B QPO seen shortly afterward, suggesting it may be an early broad precursor of the type-B QPO.
AI.motivation: To disentangle the QPO fundamental from neighboring variability components in the type-C QPO region using simultaneous PDS and CS information, and to explore whether the high-frequency shoulder is related to later type-B QPO behavior.
AI.method: Joint power-density-spectrum (PDS)–cross-spectrum (CS) decomposition applied to RXTE data, allowing separate measurement of amplitude and phase lag for the narrow QPO fundamental and a neighboring high-frequency shoulder. Includes frequency-resolved and energy-resolved fits, plus rms–energy and lag–energy analyses.
AI.result: The shoulder is first detected at MJD 54142.04 via the imaginary part of the CS and a narrow feature in the phase-lag spectrum. It tracks the QPO on the high-frequency side (R_ν ≈ 1.04–1.18). The QPO lag is small (<0.17 rad), while the shoulder shows a larger hard lag (~0.5–0.8 rad) that increases with photon energy. The rms–energy shapes of both components are broadly similar, though relative strengths evolve. The shoulder has Q ~ 2–4.
AI.conclusion: The high-frequency shoulder resembles the later type-B QPO in its lag and rms–energy behavior, suggesting it may represent an earlier, broader variability stage that later develops into the type-B QPO.

title: Gal3D: Superellipsoid Modeling of Radial 3D Galaxy Structure in IllustrisTNG and EAGLE Simulations
comment: 22 pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ. Source code: https://github.com/GalaxySimAnalytics/gal3d, and data: https://osf.io/k9x3e/
summary: Galaxy morphology and structure are key tracers of galaxy formation and evolution, making accurate measurements of intrinsic three-dimensional (3D) shape essential for linking morphology to galaxy assembly and for comparing numerical simulations. We present Gal3D, a framework that reconstructs smoothed density fields from particle data and quantifies the radial 3D structure of simulated galaxies by fitting superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces. The method recovers axis ratios, orientations, center offsets, and superellipsoid indices ($S_a$, $S_b$, $S_c$), enabling a flexible characterization of diverse galactic structures such as disks, classical bulges, box/peanut bulges, and triaxial components. Applying Gal3D to galaxies in the IllustrisTNG and EAGLE simulations, we find that the radial extent of flattened disk regions increases with stellar mass up to $M_{*,30}\sim10^{11}\,M_\odot$ and then declines sharply, with EAGLE galaxies showing a saturation at $M_{*,30}\sim10^{10.5}\,M_\odot$. The bar-related $ \varepsilon_{ab}\equiv 1-b/a$ strengthens above $M_{*,30}\sim10^{10.5}\,M_\odot$ in both simulations, but remains systematically weaker in EAGLE. In TNG, outer bar regions are commonly associated with elevated $S_a$ and $S_c$, indicating enhanced boxiness and more prominent box/peanut-shaped bulges, whereas such higher-order signatures are weak or absent in EAGLE. At the highest stellar masses, flattened disks become less prominent, while inner prolate or triaxial structures remain common and massive EAGLE galaxies have more prolate or triaxial outer stellar bodies than their TNG counterparts. These results demonstrate that Gal3D provides a practical framework for quantifying intrinsic radial 3D structure and comparing morphology across cosmological simulations.

AI.tldr: Gal3D is a framework that reconstructs smoothed density fields and fits superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces to quantify the radial 3D structure of simulated galaxies. Applied to IllustrisTNG and EAGLE, it reveals mass-dependent trends in disk extent, bar strength, boxiness, and triaxiality, showing systematic morphological differences between the two simulations.
AI.motivation: Galaxy morphology and 3D structure are key tracers of galaxy formation and evolution, but accurate measurements of intrinsic three-dimensional shapes are needed to link morphology to assembly history and compare with numerical simulations.
AI.method: Gal3D reconstructs smoothed density fields from particle data and fits superellipsoids to iso-density surfaces, recovering axis ratios, orientations, center offsets, and superellipsoid indices (Sa, Sb, Sc), which flexibly characterize disks, classical bulges, box/peanut bulges, and triaxial components. It is applied to galaxies from the IllustrisTNG and EAGLE simulations.
AI.result: The radial extent of flattened disk regions increases with stellar mass up to M*,30 ~ 10^11 Msun then declines sharply; EAGLE shows saturation at ~10^10.5 Msun. Bar-related epsilon_ab strengthens above ~10^10.5 Msun in both simulations but is systematically weaker in EAGLE.
